person.persName: عبد القادر الجيلاني ٬ محي الدين ابو محمد بن ابي صالح
ʻAbd al-Qādir al-Ǧīlānī, Muḥyī al-Dīn Abū Muḥammad b. Abī Ṣāliḥ
person.floruit: 1077-1166 A.D.Regarded as the "pole" of the eastern sufism. He was a Persian from Ǧīlān, south of the Caspian Sea. Hanbalite theologian, preacher and ṣūfī, who gave his name to the ṣufī order of the Qādiriyya; he's considered to be the greatest saint of Islam. Baghdad, where he came to study at the age of eighteen, remained the scene of his activities up to his death. After completing his education in taṣawwuf, tafsīr and fiqh, al-Ǧīlānī left Baghdad. He spent twenty-five years as a reclusive wanderer in the desert regions of Iraq. In 1127 al-Ǧīlānī returned to Baghdad and began to preach to the public. He died in the evening of 8 Rabī‘ al-Awwal 561 H, at the age of eighty nine years; his body was entombed in a shrine within his madrasa on the East bank of the Tigris in Baghdad, Iraq. During the reign of the Safavid Shah Isma‘īl I, al-Ǧīlānī's shrine was destroyed, however in 1535 the Ottoman Sultan Sulaymān had a turba built over the shrine, which exists to this day. As one of the greatest saint of Islam he's addressee of various du‘ā' and subject of many example of devotional literature.
